## FAQ

### What are some alternatives to Framer?

Webflow, WordPress.com, Squarespace, Wix, Figma Sites, Durable, Dorik, Unicorn Platform and Carrd are all alternatives to Framer website builder plans with a tier priced under Pro, compared yearly with yearly and monthly with monthly. Webflow suits big CMS sites, WordPress.com adds plugins, Durable and Dorik build with AI, and Carrd covers single landing pages.

### Which Framer alternative costs the least? [...] | Your situation | Start with | Why |

| A content-heavy site with a big CMS | Webflow Premium | 40 collections and 20,000 items |

Framer has a loyal following, but users can be seen flagging the same issues once they try to push it beyond a polished landing page. results.content:
That makes it the right call for campaign microsites, brand pages, and portfolio-style storytelling where every scroll and hover needs to feel intentional. Use it when your team's biggest question is "does this look premium," not "does this handle user accounts."

Once your roadmap adds logins, dashboards, or role-based permissions, Framer stops being the right foundation.

### Webstudio: Best open-source alternative

Webstudio is the best fit when your team needs open-source control and the ability to self-host rather than depend on a proprietary platform.

Its open-source codebase means you can inspect it, modify it, and deploy it on your own infrastructure, which gives you extensibility a closed builder can't match and cuts your platform lock-in significantly. [...] ## Best Webflow alternatives by use case

The best Webflow alternative is whichever platform's architecture matches your site's job, your team's skills, and how much ownership you want over the stack. Building an app, polishing a marketing site, wanting an open-source Webflow alternative, launching fast as a startup, or running a content-heavy publication all point to different tools.

The five Webflow competitors below, Bolt.new, Framer, Webstudio, Wix, and WordPress, get compared the same way: best fit, core strength, application-layer capability, and the tradeoff you're accepting.

### Bolt.new: Best for teams building web apps with AI [...] Try this prompt: "Build a client portal with email/password login, a dashboard showing project status, and a database storing client records." Review the preview, refine sections by prompting again, connect your database, then deploy straight from Bolt.new without adding separate vendors.

### Framer: Best for design-focused marketing sites

Framer is the best fit when your site's job is to look polished and move fluidly, not run application logic. It's built around a design-first workflow, with drag-and-drop layouts, real interaction states, and motion that feels native rather than bolted on.

results.title: The open-source Framer and Webflow alternative – with Webstudio
results.content:
Framer costs some serious money too, although the Basic Plan for $15 per month gives you access to one CMS collection, meaning creating a website with a blog is a bit cheaper with Framer compared to Webflow. The biggest drawbacks of Framer is that you are not able to export the CMS, the CMS itself is quite limited, and you are not getting the cleanest code in case you want to export your website. For Webflow, the biggest drawback might be indeed the costs.

While we have been talking about Framer and Webflow a lot until now, this post is about a new contender entering the area of visual development. The tool I am dedicating this deep dive to is privacy-focused, open-source, lets you connect your frontend to any backend, and avoid hosting lock-in. Let me introduce you to Webstudio\. [...] In case you want to make the switch from Webflow, Webstudio gives you the possibility to copy from Webflow and paste into Webstudio to translate your work into components and styles. This applies to Webflow projects, templates, and component libraries, which means you can start your next project with one of the 1,000s of free (or paid) Webflow templates, and then copy each page and paste it into Webstudio to continue building it there. To give you an even more streamlined start with Webstudio, it gives you access to Radix UI components, an open-source components library optimized for fast development, easy maintenance, and accessibility.

### So, how does Webstudio compare to Framer and Webflow? [...] However, it already offers a great set of features and functionality, it is open-source providing the superior trajectory compared to Framer and Webflow, it has the most advanced CMS as it gives you the possibility to use any headless CMS instead of being locked into a solution that does not really fit your needs, and it is the cheaper option compared to the quite high pricing of Webflow.

There is no one-size-fits-all solution, but Webstudio\ indeed checks off a lot of boxes.

Till next time! 👋‌‌‌‌
